articles.title: Galaxies in a cosmic house of mirrors
articles.description:
Image:
			
This NASA/ESA/CSA James Webb Space Telescope Picture of the Month features galaxies in great detail that have been warped and multiplied like they’ve stepped into a house of mirrors. The brilliant golden galaxies splashed across this image belong to a galaxy cluster called MACS J0454.1-0300. The orange galaxies concentrated on one side of the cluster are not actually part of the cluster and are much farther away from us.
MACS J0454.1-0300 is itself immensely distant: the light from these galaxies has been travelling to us for so long that we’re seeing the cluster as it was when the Universe was about 8 billion years old. While this galaxy cluster is a valuable scientific target in its own right, the real stars of this image are the galaxies that appear warped and stretched, like a painting that has been smeared by a giant hand.
The way these galaxies look is the result of gravitational lensing, in which the enormous mass of a foreground object such as a galaxy cluster bends and magnifies the light from a more distant object in the background. Gravitational lensing allows astronomers to observe galaxies, star clusters and even individual stars that are too far away for our telescopes to see under normal conditions. While the large, orange galaxies appear obviously distorted, look carefully at some of the small reddish background galaxies throughout this picture: even at the very edges of the frame, there are galaxies whose images have been bent into tiny arcs by MACS J0454.1-0300’s gravity.
The gravitationally lensed areas show multiple images of galaxies from when the Universe was young: a group of galaxies 2 billion years after the Big Bang, and a single galaxy just 800 million years old after the Big Bang. The galaxy group appears to be going through a merger, resulting in an enormous burst of star formation.
Astronomers have also identified individual bright ‘knots’ within the gravitationally lensed areas, corresponding to regions as small as 5 light-years across. These tiny clumps appear magnified by a factor of more than 300, in some cases.
A NASA/ESA Hubble Space Telescope image of this same cluster was released in 2014. Take a moment to compare the two images; the difference between them is dramatic. The new Webb image reveals hundreds of galaxies missing from the earlier image. These galaxies were there all along, but Webb is much more sensitive to their much redder light.
The data behind this image come from two observing programmes (#5058, PI: Furtak; #6882, PI: Fujimoto) that leverage the ability of massive galaxy clusters to bring distant objects into view.
[Image Description: A massive galaxy cluster, made of many golden elliptical galaxies with the largest, brightest one in the centre. Heavily distorted orange galaxies appear all around the cluster, the largest concentrated in a large arc around the cluster's centre; these are images of very distant galaxies, created by gravitational lensing. A few galaxies are large and bluish-white in colour; bright, nearby stars are the same colour.]
Release on esawebb.org
articles.summary: The James Webb Space Telescope captures galaxies with unprecedented detail through gravitational lensing effects, revealing cosmic structures with remarkable clarity. This breakthrough observation showcases the power of modern astronomical instruments.

articles.title: BepiColombo’s Mercury arrival begins - full replay
articles.description:
Video: 
			02:31:10
				
Watch the replay of the livestream originally broadcast on 3 September as ESA/JAXA's BepiColombo mission took the first critical step towards arriving at Mercury.
After travelling through the inner Solar System together for eight years, BepiColombo's Mercury Transfer Module (MTM) will separate from the rest of the stacked spacecraft on 3 September 2026. This marks the beginning of one of the most complex planetary arrival sequences ever attempted by ESA.
Broadcast live from ESA's European Space Operations Centre (ESOC) in Darmstadt, Germany, the programme includes live views from the iconic Main Control Room, expert analysis, behind-the-scenes insights, and the first signal from the spacecraft following separation. 
Livestream schedule (CEST): 

13:45 – Livestream begins 
16:00-16:45 – End of livestream
articles.summary: BepiColombo successfully arrived at Mercury on September 3, marking a historic achievement in planetary exploration by the ESA and JAXA. The livestream replay documents this remarkable milestone in humanity's exploration of the inner solar system.

articles.title: NASA's First Selection for a New Class of Mission: The PRIMA Far-Infrared Telescope
articles.description: NASA announced Wednesday a mission to explore the history and evolution of the universe, PRIMA (PRobe far-Infrared Mission for Astrophysics), is advancing to the next phase of development. This space telescope is the first in a new class of NASA astrophysics missions, called Probe Explorers, within the agency’s longstanding Explorers Program.
articles.summary: NASA has selected the PRIMA far-infrared telescope mission to explore the history and evolution of the universe with unprecedented infrared sensitivity. This groundbreaking mission will unlock secrets of cosmic history and stellar birth.

articles.title: NASA’s Roman telescope just opened its planet-hunting eye
articles.description: NASA’s Roman Space Telescope has demonstrated remarkable pointing stability and given its powerful planet-imaging coronagraph its first look at the cosmos. The telescope can already stay locked on a target with precision comparable to aiming a laser at a dime from about 150 miles away. Its coronagraph also captured stars in the Large Magellanic Cloud, confirming that the instrument can produce focused images.
articles.summary: NASA's Roman Space Telescope demonstrates exceptional pointing stability and successfully tests its revolutionary planet-hunting coronagraph.

articles.title: Powerful simulations reveal how the first stars changed the universe
articles.description: Ultra-detailed simulations are showing how the first stars lit up the dark Universe and seeded space with elements such as carbon, oxygen, and iron. The MEGATRON project could bridge JWST observations of the earliest galaxies with chemical clues preserved in ancient stars today.
articles.summary: Ultra-detailed simulations show how the first stars illuminated the dark universe and distributed the elements necessary for planets and life.

articles.title: La semaine intense de SpaceX : toutes ses fusées utilisées, première orbite du Starship, record américain de vitesse vers l’ISS et mission top secrète
articles.description: SpaceX a lancé ses trois modèles de fusées en moins de quatre jours. Le Starship est parti ce lundi 28 septembre, puis deux Falcon 9 et une Falcon Heavy ont décollé en moins de 13 heures, entre ce jeudi 1er octobre et la nuit suivante. Pour la première fois, …
articles.summary: SpaceX launches all three rocket models within four days, including Starship's first orbital flight and record-breaking ISS delivery speed. This remarkable achievement demonstrates unprecedented momentum in commercial spaceflight.

articles.title: Science begins for Smile
articles.description: On 23 September, the European-Chinese Smile mission was declared ready to start revealing how Earth responds to the wind of charged particles from the Sun. This follows a busy in-space commissioning period since the spacecraft launched on 19 May and reached its target orbit for science operations on 20 June.
articles.summary: The European-Chinese Smile mission has been declared ready to begin observations of how Earth's magnetosphere responds to solar wind interactions. This landmark mission promises new insights into planetary magnetic dynamics.

articles.title: Successful Earth flyby improves Juice’s course to Jupiter
articles.description: The European Space Agency’s Jupiter Icy Moons Explorer (Juice) skimmed the very outer edge of Earth’s atmosphere on 28 September, using the gravity of our home planet to alter its route to Jupiter using very little fuel.
articles.summary: The European Space Agency's Juice spacecraft successfully performed an Earth gravity assist maneuver on September 28, fine-tuning its trajectory toward Jupiter's icy moons. This successful flyby demonstrates precise mission planning and execution.

articles.title: Asteroid Bennu Has an Identity Crisis, and Jupiter Might Be to Blame
articles.description: Asteroid sample return missions have brought well preserved samples of the early solar system (that hadn’t been roasted in a fireball) back to Earth for the first time. But those samples, like the OSIRIS-REx sample from asteroid (101955) Bennu, sometimes provide more questions than answers. A new paper, published in Science Advances from researchers at ETH Zurich and Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory, highlights one of those questions - why Bennu appears to have been born in both the inner and outer solar system - and a possible answer to it.
articles.summary: Analysis of samples from asteroid Bennu reveals unexpected compositional variations that may trace back to Jupiter's early gravitational influence on the solar system. This discovery provides new insights into planetary migration and early solar system dynamics.

articles.title: NASA's Hubble Marks its 200,000th Orbit by Watching Lensed Supernova
articles.description: NASA’s Hubble Space Telescope completed its 200,000th orbit around Earth on Sept. 19th and marked this milestone with observations that could help refine astronomers' measurements of cosmic expansion (aka. the Hubble Constant).
articles.summary: The Hubble Space Telescope celebrates its 200,000th orbit by observing a gravitationally lensed supernova, demonstrating continued scientific excellence after decades of service. This milestone reflects Hubble's enduring legacy as one of humanity's greatest scientific instruments.

articles.title: First Direct Image of Protoplanet Swirling Surrounding Gas
articles.description: The formation and evolution of planets is the driving force behind both where and how we might find life beyond Earth. This complex and lengthy process first begins with a massive ball of gas and dust that swirls until it flattens into a disk, followed by rocks ranging in size from pebbles to kilometer-scale objects clumping together in a process known as accretion, as they too swirl around within the larger disk and form rocky planets closer to the star and the farther out planets collect the gas, ice, and dust that the star couldn’t evaporate. Until now, researchers have been limited to visualizing the swirling gas and dust forming planets through computer models.
articles.summary: Astronomers have obtained the first direct image of a protoplanet surrounded by its planet-forming disk, revealing the birth process of new worlds. This breakthrough observation provides unprecedented insight into planetary formation mechanisms.

articles.title: Coldest Lava Exoplanet Found to Hold an Atmosphere
articles.description: Exoplanets continue to challenge our understanding of planetary formation, evolution, and whether they might be able to support life as we know it. Scientists often use planets in our solar system as analogs for exoplanets, studying exoplanets with extremely short orbital periods forces scientists to constantly rethink our understanding of what planets can withstand during their lifetimes. One such type of exoplanet that has entered the foray in recent years are “lava world” exoplanets, and especially lava exoplanets that orbit dangerously close to their stars. But while it has been long known that lava worlds on with higher temperatures have atmospheres, “colder” lava worlds have been found to lack atmospheres.
articles.summary: Scientists discover that an unusually cool lava exoplanet retains an atmosphere despite its extreme surface conditions, challenging conventional models of planetary evolution. This discovery expands our understanding of what kinds of worlds can sustain atmospheres.

articles.title: Gamma-ray search sets new limits on dark matter annihilation in the inner Milky Way
articles.description: Dark matter could be a type of matter in the universe that does not emit, absorb or reflect detectable light and appears to interact very weakly with regular matter. Although physicists have observed gravitational effects attributed to dark matter, they have not yet been able to determine what it is made of.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: New gamma-ray observations establish unprecedented limits on dark matter annihilation in the inner Milky Way, advancing our understanding of this cosmic mystery.

articles.title: Hidden X-ray phase revealed in likely neutron star merger
articles.description: An international team of astronomers, including researchers from the Department of Physics and the Hong Kong Institute for Astronomy and Astrophysics (HKIAA) at The University of Hong Kong (HKU), has discovered a previously hidden phase of high-energy activity following the merger of compact stars.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Astronomers discover a hidden X-ray phase in a likely neutron star merger, revealing new insights into these extreme cosmic collisions.

articles.title: How Enceladus' ocean spray becomes chemically diverse ice grains
articles.description: Saturn's icy moon Enceladus hides a global ocean beneath its frozen surface. From fractures near its south pole, material from this ocean is ejected into space as a plume of water vapor and ice particles. These particles offer scientists a rare opportunity to investigate an extraterrestrial ocean without drilling through kilometers of ice.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Research reveals how Enceladus' subsurface ocean spray produces chemically diverse ice grains, offering clues to the moon's habitability potential.

articles.title: Milky Way may have begun as thousands of galaxies, new simulations suggest
articles.description: In the early days of the universe, our home looked very different from how it does today. Back then, the region in our universe that would eventually become our Milky Way neighborhood was a collection of thousands of smaller galaxies—some pumping out tons of new stars, others filled only with gas or littered with dead stars and black holes.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: New simulations suggest the early Milky Way formed from thousands of smaller galaxies rather than emerging as a single entity.

articles.title: Team selected for NASA program to explore potential lunar cave
articles.description: NASA has selected a Planetary Science Institute–led proposal to investigate whether a potentially large underground cave extends beyond the opening of a lunar pit. Such a cave may one day provide a safe haven for astronauts to escape the radiation and extreme temperature swings present at the lunar surface.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: NASA selects a team to explore a potentially large underground cave on the Moon, advancing lunar exploration capabilities.

articles.title: Black holes may grow quietly alongside galaxies even without violent mergers
articles.description: Astronomers analyzed 2,435 galaxies hosting actively feeding black holes using data from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI). Among them, they identified 546 "bulgeless" galaxies—systems with little or no central stellar bulge. Their paper, published in Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society, suggests that galaxies without a central bulge grow black holes just as effectively as galaxies that have one—a surprising sign that black holes don't need galaxy mergers to grow normally.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Analysis of thousands of galaxies reveals that black holes can grow steadily alongside their host galaxies without requiring violent mergers.

articles.title: Scientists find a surprising clue to why the universe’s expansion doesn’t add up
articles.description: Tiny magnetic fields created shortly after the Big Bang may help explain the long-running disagreement over how fast the universe is expanding. Detailed simulations show that these primordial fields could have changed the formation of hydrogen in the early universe, affecting the cosmic microwave background and the expansion rate inferred from it.
articles.summary: Magnetic fields created shortly after the Big Bang may help resolve the long-standing puzzle of the universe's expansion rate discrepancy.

articles.title: ESA’s Juice just used Earth as a slingshot to Jupiter
articles.description: ESA’s Juice spacecraft raced past Earth on September 28, using our planet’s gravity to dramatically reshape its path toward Jupiter without burning much fuel. The flyby changed its direction by 20 degrees and increased its speed by 3.5 km/s, while also giving scientists a rare chance to test its instruments on Earth and the Moon.
articles.summary: ESA's Juice spacecraft successfully uses Earth's gravity as a slingshot to reshape its trajectory toward Jupiter exploration.

articles.title: Chang’e-6 lunar soil contains a surprising magnetic time capsule
articles.description: Scientists studying Chang’e-6 lunar soil have discovered a previously unknown magnetic mineral in natural Moon samples: a form of metallic iron called γ-Fe. Found inside tiny impact-glass particles, the nanoscale iron can preserve a stable magnetic signal, potentially acting like a microscopic fossil of the Moon’s long-lost magnetic field.
articles.summary: Chang'e-6 lunar samples contain a previously unknown magnetic mineral, revealing new insights into the Moon's geological and magnetic history.

articles.title: The early universe wasn’t nearly as pristine as scientists thought
articles.description: JWST has revealed that galaxies were spreading carbon, oxygen, and other heavy elements through space just 500 million years after the Big Bang. The surprising discovery suggests the young universe became chemically enriched much earlier than expected, potentially erasing traces of its very first stars.
articles.summary: JWST observations reveal that the early universe was more chemically complex than previously thought, with galaxies distributing heavy elements like carbon and oxygen just 500 million years after the Big Bang.

articles.title: The Universe Is Full of Tiny Red Dots—and They’re One of Astronomy’s Biggest Discoveries in Decades
articles.description: A new type of object found in the early universe has puzzled astronomers for years, but they may finally have some answers.
articles.summary: Astronomers have identified a new class of mysterious objects in the early universe—tiny red dots—that represent one of the most significant astronomical discoveries in recent decades.

articles.title: NASA 宣布最新遠紅外線望遠鏡 PRIMA 計畫，探索星球形成與材料之謎
articles.description:
恆星如何從厚重的塵埃誕生？行星水又從哪裡來？NASA 宣布新遠紅外線太空望遠鏡 PRIMA（PRobe far-Infrared Mission for Astrophysics，意為「天文物理遠紅外線探測任務」）獲選進入下階段開發，目標 2033 年發射，展開為期五年觀測。

這項任務源自天文學界 2020 年對未來十年研究方向的整體建議，規模介於小型探索任務與大型旗艦望遠鏡之間，希望補足現有設備的觀測能力。目前 PRIMA 將進行初步設計與技術開發，之後若通過確認審查，專案成本上限為 12 億美元，不含發射…
articles.summary: NASA announces the PRIMA mission, a far-infrared space telescope selected for development that will investigate stellar formation and the origins of planetary water.

articles.title: ISS : la relève est arrivée, Sophie Adenot va revenir sur Terre avec un beau record en poche
articles.description: La fin approche pour Sophie Adenot. Après plus de sept mois en orbite, l’astronaute française reviendra bientôt sur Terre dans une capsule Crew Dragon. Un séjour qui a marqué l’histoire tricolore à plus d’un titre.
articles.summary: French astronaut Sophie Adenot completes over seven months aboard the International Space Station and returns to Earth with a notable spaceflight record. Her mission exemplifies the remarkable achievements of modern human spaceflight programs.

articles.title: Reise zur Raumstation: Besatzung der Crew-13 erreicht ISS in Rekordzeit
articles.description: So schnell klappte es noch nie: In weniger als acht Stunden nach dem Start erreicht die Dragon-Kapsel von SpaceX mit der Crew-13 die Internationale Raumstation im Erdorbit.
articles.summary: SpaceX's Dragon capsule reaches the International Space Station in under eight hours, setting a new speed record for crewed missions. This breakthrough showcases advances in rapid-transit human spaceflight.

articles.title: Is SpaceX's Starship The Most Powerful Rocket Ever Built?
articles.description: SpaceX fitted Starship's first-stage booster with 33 engines, enough to make you wonder how it compares with the most powerful rockets humans have ever built.
articles.summary: SpaceX's Starship first-stage booster features 33 engines, establishing it as a contender for most powerful rocket ever built. This engineering marvel represents a leap forward in launch capability.

articles.title: Rocket Report: SpaceX completes launch triple-header; Rocket Lab nets big contract
articles.description:
Welcome to Edition 9.13 of the Rocket Report!
This week, SpaceX celebrated the first orbital launch of its new Starship rocket. I’m not sure many people, at least those outside of SpaceX, expected it to take 14 flights of Starship before it technically reache…
articles.summary: SpaceX completes a triple-header launch week featuring Starship's historic first orbital flight and Rocket Lab secures major contracts. The space industry achieves unprecedented operational tempo.

articles.title: SpaceX launches 4 astronauts on a fast track to the International Space Station
articles.description: Four astronauts have arrived at the International Space Station following an express eight-hour flight.
articles.summary: Four astronauts reach the International Space Station via an express eight-hour flight, setting a new benchmark for rapid crewed spaceflight. This achievement showcases SpaceX's ability to safely and efficiently transport humans to orbit.

articles.title: Win a trip to ESA to witness BepiColombo arrive at Mercury
articles.description:
Get ready to celebrate BepiColombo’s arrival at Mercury. Craft a welcoming message that could be a drawing, song, poem or any other art form and stand a chance to win a trip to mission control! 
ENTRY FORM  
Full rules and how to enter below.
articles.summary: The ESA invites the public to contribute creative messages welcoming BepiColombo's arrival at Mercury, celebrating this landmark achievement with global participation. This engagement opportunity inspires wonder about planetary exploration.
